answer: To bid for juniper permits in a karst reserve, each key locks 40 credits until the auction closes. A cipher hides each bid until the reveal window. The contract checks that every sealed bid has its own escrow before admitting it and forfeits bonds for bids left unopened. One honest bidder locks 40 refundable credits. A farm submitting 1,000 bids at once must lock 40,000, even if it funds all keys from one wallet. It can reveal all bids and recover the bonds, so the deterrent is capital tied up. Honest bidders also lose access to their funds during the auction.
